item.title: A deep dive into pstack
item.content:encoded: pstack turns Cursor into a rigorous engineering workflow with playbooks, specialist skills, multi-model review, and runtime verification.

item.title: How to use Herdr skills and herdr --skill
item.content:encoded: Learn how to install the Herdr agent skill, use herdr --skill, and let coding agents safely inspect, split, run, and wait in panes.

item.title: JavaScript immutable array methods: toSorted(), toReversed(), toSpliced(), with()
item.content:encoded: Need to sort or reverse an array without mutating it? Use toSorted(), toReversed(), toSpliced(), and with() to get a new copy instead.

item.title: Native CSS Nesting
item.content:encoded: Native CSS nesting works without Sass. Learn basic nesting, the ampersand selector, nested media queries, specificity gotchas, and when to drop preprocessors.

item.title: The View Transitions API
item.content:encoded: Create smooth same-document animations with the View Transitions API using startViewTransition, CSS pseudo-elements, and view-transition-name on elements.

item.title: MutationObserver and ResizeObserver
item.content:encoded: Use MutationObserver to watch DOM changes and ResizeObserver to track element size changes, with practical examples and cleanup via disconnect().

item.title: The Popover API
item.content:encoded: Build native browser popovers with the Popover API using HTML attributes, auto and manual modes, CSS backdrop styling, and JavaScript show and hide methods.

item.title: Find command-line tools from a macOS app
item.content:encoded: Fix tools that work in Terminal but disappear from Finder-launched macOS apps by locating binaries and building an explicit child-process PATH.

item.title: The HTML dialog tag
item.content:encoded: Learn the native HTML dialog element for accessible modals: showModal, close, form method dialog, backdrop styling, and why it beats div modals.

item.title: The CSS :has() selector
item.content:encoded: The CSS parent selector styles an element from what is inside it. Forms, cards, previous siblings, quantity queries, and when JavaScript is still better.

item.title: What I learned reading Claude's system prompts
item.content:encoded: I read Anthropic's published Claude system prompts. Most of the product lives in the rules, facts, tools, and safety checks around the model.

item.title: CSS Container Queries
item.content:encoded: CSS container queries style a component by its own width, not the viewport. Learn container-type, named containers, query units, and the traps that break layouts.

item.title: Add a local LLM without making your app depend on it
item.content:encoded: Add optional Ollama-generated summaries to a Swift app while preserving deterministic fallback data, short health checks, failure backoff, caching, and testability.

item.title: AbortController: how to cancel a fetch request in JavaScript
item.content:encoded: Learn how to cancel fetch requests in JavaScript with AbortController, handle AbortError, set timeouts, and abort on unmount or superseded requests.

item.title: The Intersection Observer API
item.content:encoded: An in-depth tutorial on the Intersection Observer API: entries, thresholds, rootMargin, lazy loading, infinite scroll, scrollspy, visibility tracking, and the pitfalls to avoid.

item.title: Cloudflare AI Gateway: put a proxy in front of your LLM calls
item.content:encoded: Learn how Cloudflare AI Gateway sits between your application and AI models, then route and inspect a real request through a Worker.

item.title: Cloudflare Workers AI: run LLMs without API keys
item.content:encoded: Learn what Cloudflare Workers AI is, connect its AI binding to a Worker, and build a small text summarization API step by step.

item.title: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3: what changed and why it matters
item.content:encoded: Learn how HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 changed connections, multiplexing, compression, QUIC, deployment, and the web performance decisions you make today.

item.title: WebAssembly tutorial
item.content:encoded: Learn WebAssembly step by step by compiling a small module, loading it from JavaScript, and working with exports, imports, and memory.

item.title: A deep dive into cmux
item.content:encoded: Learn how cmux combines terminals, browsers, notifications, SSH, session restore, and automation into one native workspace for coding agents.

item.title: What your photos leak: EXIF metadata and GPS
item.content:encoded: Many photos embed EXIF metadata such as GPS coordinates, timestamps, and device information. Learn what it stores, who strips it, and how to check.

item.title: A deep dive into HTMX
item.content:encoded: Learn how HTMX turns HTML attributes into requests and DOM swaps, with forms, partials, events, history, security, debugging, and real Astro projects.

item.title: A deep dive into open-weight AI models
item.content:encoded: Learn what AI model weights are, what open-weight releases let you do, how local inference works, and why open weights are not always open source.

item.title: A deep dive into Hono
item.content:encoded: Follow one request through Hono to see how routing, middleware, context, Web Standards, and runtime adapters work together.

item.title: Herdr vs cmux: which one should you use?
item.content:encoded: Compare Herdr and cmux for coding agents: persistence, agent state, macOS UX, browser automation, SSH, and multi-agent workflows.

item.title: A deep dive into Kysely
item.content:encoded: Build a small PostgreSQL-backed store with Kysely, from the first typed query to joins, transactions, migrations, debugging, and tests.

item.title: A deep dive into Cloudflare Computer
item.content:encoded: How Cloudflare Computer combines a Durable Object filesystem, Dynamic Worker runtimes, a container backend, FUSE mount, and sync protocol.

item.title: A deep dive into Herdr
item.content:encoded: Herdr keeps coding agents in persistent terminal workspaces, shows which ones need attention, and exposes the whole system through a CLI and API.

item.title: Glob patterns explained (and why .gitignore behaves that way)
item.content:encoded: How glob patterns work: star vs double star, question marks, character classes, brace expansion, and the gitignore rules that trip everyone up.

item.title: Deploying Hono on Cloudflare Workers
item.content:encoded: Deploy a Hono API on Cloudflare Workers with wrangler dev, typed D1 bindings, and a tiny REST endpoint. The final post in the Bun and Hono series.
